headline: The Tipu Short is a day overdue and the Guru Tegh Bahadur Short, due 24 November, has no script either: script Tegh Bahadur today. The Indonesia long-form is past day three with 71,382 views, and its first subscribers run at 3.4 per 1,000 against 2 for the Asia one, so the Bali follow-up stays.

top3.topic: Tipu Sultan: a day overdue, no script
top3.signal: Due on 20 November, the calendar's date for him. The Tipu Jayanti row (News18 Marathi) has been in the news for three days.
top3.recommendation: Script it straight after Tegh Bahadur and publish by 22 November, or press Drop on the Today tab. It lapses on 23 November.

top3.topic: The Malay Ramayana Short: already cut, not on YouTube
top3.signal: The Short on Ravana getting his powers from Allah has been on Instagram since 20 November but not on YouTube. Its script was written to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form, which runs at 801.5 views an hour.
top3.recommendation: Upload it as a YouTube Short today or tomorrow, title starting with “Ravana”, with the Indonesia long-form as its related video, and keep 23 November clear for Tegh Bahadur. That it sends viewers to the long-form is a guess.

top3.signal: The top date on the radar, three days out. The radar's step this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. The calendar flags the martyrdom framing as one to avoid.
top3.recommendation: Script today, record on 22 November, publish on 23 November at about 17:00 IST. Judge it on day three, 26 November, and on search over the year, by the channel's own lesson: “Persecution memory with a named defender, released on its anniversary, earns search traffic for a year; judge it on lifetime search views, not on day-three feed widening.”

more.signal: Nine days out. The radar's step this week is to research him with named sources and script a Short on the colonial mechanism: who ordered it, who profited, what the British record itself admits.
more.recommendation: Only if a slot opens after Tegh Bahadur: one Short on the Bengal famine of 1943, convicted from British papers (the War Cabinet record, Leo Amery's diary), checked before recording, published on 30 November. The channel's earlier Churchill Short failed on this lesson: “The one-sentence context rule applies inside the first 10 seconds most of all.”

skipped.signal: On the radar for the same date as Tegh Bahadur (from an on-this-day list), and the Tarabai Short is one of the channel's four breakouts.
skipped.recommendation: Skip. Two Shorts on one date split one sitting, and Tegh Bahadur has the bigger searched name. The breakout set Tarabai against Aurangzeb; this is a Maratha court quarrel with no outside villain.

skipped.topic: Rajiv and Indira Gandhi on Wikipedia
skipped.signal: English readership of Rajiv Gandhi at 3.19x its 30-day median and Indira Gandhi at 2.22x, with the Emergency and Indira Gandhi in the news all week.
skipped.recommendation: Skip until the Sonia Gandhi Short has its day three on 23 November (655 views so far). Shorts on recent politics have landed below the usual here, so another would rest on the spike alone.

whats_working: “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is the month's long-form: 71,382 views in 89 hours, 801.5 an hour against 301 for the Asia long-form over its life, a like rate of 1.8% against 0.9%, and viewers writing “Great video, subscribed!” under it.
Long-form still brings most of what uploads bring: 79.2% of upload net subscribers over 28 days (511 against 134 from Shorts), on 44.4% of upload views.

The best converter in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 13.3 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the Tegh Bahadur Short's shape: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” Here that means who gave the order and what the record says, checked before recording.
whats_wrong: Neither dated Short has a script on disk: Tipu was due on 20 November and Tegh Bahadur's script was due today. Probable cause: the owner's own picks fill the week (the Sonia Gandhi Short on 20 November, the Param Vir Chakra script the same day, the ICS salaries Short reopened on 19 November). Test: none, it is a choice. Script Tegh Bahadur first, because its date will not move.

Reach is not turning into subscribers at the old rate: the Indonesia long-form 3.4 per 1,000 views and the Asia one 2, against 8.3 for long-form over the channel's life. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing. 195,639 long-form views over 28 days came from the Home and subscriptions bucket against 5,572 from search, and only 41.4% of November's long-form views were engaged views. Test: the Indonesia video has no transcript in the script library, so the check of where its viewers left could not run; add it (see housekeeping) before writing the Bali script.

Shorts views fell 58.0% week over week to 2026-11-18. Probable cause: the Ravana film Shorts' run of 11 November left the window and nothing dated replaced it; the later film Shorts, “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule” (1,703 views) and “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?” (1,392), stayed below the usual. Search no longer carries Shorts either: it brought 30.1% of Shorts views over 28 days, out of its usual range. Test: the Tegh Bahadur Short's first three days.

actions.action: Reply under the Majapahit correction on “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus”: what Majapahit's court worshipped, and that the Adam-and-Allah version is the Malay Hikayat Seri Rama. Keep the current pinned comment. /replies drafts it.
actions.rationale: The video is still climbing, so every new viewer reads its top comments, and the correction is among the most liked. That a reply helps is a guess.

actions.action: Put the Indonesia long-form's final script or transcript in the long-form scripts folder so the next refresh can show where its viewers left.
actions.rationale: Its drop-off check could not run without it, and the Bali script should be written knowing where this one lost people.

actions.action: If not done yet, put the Indonesia long-form on the end screen of “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”.
actions.rationale: The Asia long-form has 159,865 views on the same subject. The Indonesia video's pinned comment links back to it, but the Asia one's pinned comment shows no link the other way. That it helps is a guess.

actions.action: If not done yet, check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” has 2 views since 3 November.
actions.rationale: A public Short gets at least a handful of views, so none at all points to its visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.

actions.action: Ask the designer for a second thumbnail for “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” and run a Test & Compare in Studio.
actions.rationale: It is the best converter over the 365-day window: 34.2 subscribers per 1,000 views on only 1,082 views: the people who find it subscribe, too few find it.

growth.verdict: Needs 225 net subscribers a day. The channel does 52.88/day, so the target is a **4.2x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "1. Current rate, nothing changes"), reaches 52.9/day — still 4.2x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2031-02-19, 4.2 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1279 of the 3,006 subscribers that 22 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 26.5/day (742 of 1,375 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 22 long-form and 104 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.3 more long-form videos a year — 39.3 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 33 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 137, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 457 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 26.5/day (742 of 1,375 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 9 revision long-form videos, median 69 subscribers, against 33 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 26.5/day (742 of 1,375 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,279 subscribers on 73,021 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
